messages:
nina: Noticed a sudden drop in KV prefix cache hit rate after last night's attn compiler rollout (attn-compiler-v3). Baseline ~0.86 -> nightly ~0.68. Short-chat routes hit hardest.

sam: Oof. Any immediate traces/metrics to share?

nina: Pulled the runtime hist and logs. p50 short prompt latency +90ms, KV_CACHE_HIT metric went 0.86->0.68. Link to perf alert: https://perf.internal/alerts/AC-489

perf-bot: alert: prefix_cache_hitrate deviation (p99). job: telemetry/prefixcache/nightly-eval/2024-06-18

leo: Can we see the computed KV key bytes for two consecutive identical prefixes on both builds? If the key bytes differ, that's the root cause.

nina: I instrumented a quick build and grabbed raw key bytes. Pre-rollout: key_raw=af12b3c4d5e6f7
Post-rollout: key_raw=af12b3c4d5e6f7||00:comp=v3-7a2d (literal suffix).

ashley: Wait, literal suffix? That sounds like the compiler appended a build tag when serializing the normalized prefix. Was there a debug flag enabled in the new pipeline?

sam: I checked the compile flags used by the attn CI job: --kv-attach-buildtag=true was toggled on in the v3 rollout config to help correlate cache entries to compile ids. Looks like that was left on in the production build.

leo: That would explain consistent hash differences — same prefix bytes but with appended compile tag, so lookup always misses older entries. Why would we append it at serialization time? That should be metadata, not part of canonical key.

nina: Repro curl for the test pattern I ran (5k reqs same prefix):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
  -d '{"model":"attn-v3-quant","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<fixed-system>"},{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Ran loop 5000x and scraped runtime metrics.

sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) Flip --kv-attach-buildtag=false in the compiler rollout (hotfix), 2) Add a runtime lookup shim that strips known suffix patterns from serialized key before digesting, 3) Run a backfill to reindex cache entries with new keys.

ashley: For Dedicated customers we should avoid silently changing key formats. Rolling back flag on nightly first makes sense. Also add an invariant test in CI to assert canonicalization does not include compile metadata bytes.

nina: I pushed a canary with --kv-attach-buildtag=false to canary-3 pool and re-ran the 5k test. Canary hit_rate=0.85 vs nightly 0.69. So flipping the flag fixes lookup.

perf-bot: canary job update: telemetry/prefixcache/canary-3/2024-06-18: before=0.69 canary=0.85 baseline=0.86

sam: I'll prepare a small runtime shim that strips trailing patterns like "||00:comp=*" and also ignore any trailing nulls. This should restore hits for mixed caches while we coordinate a clean rollback. PR incoming.

leo: Also add a unit test to the kernel serialization tests: for a given input token sequence, serialized canonical bytes must be identical across compiler versions unless an explicit compatibility-breaking flag is set. Fail pipeline if not.

nina: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/compiler/pulls/5432 (flip flag) and https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2179 (strip-suffix-shim). Runtime PR has microbench + metric cache_key_posthoc_strip_count.

ashley: I'll file infra job to run a controlled reindex/migration for Dedicated pools that can't tolerate mixed-format lookups: JIRA RT-1337. Include opt-out toggles.

sam: Patch landed in runtime CI branch. Quick perf microbench shows minimal CPU impact for the strip shim (~0.4% added latency on key compute).

nina: After canary rollout and landing the compile flag revert, nightly was re-run. KV_CACHE_HIT returned to 0.84 within 30 minutes on the rolled pool. We should still schedule the migration and CI tests before full fleet rollout.

perf-bot: summary: root cause = compiler flag (--kv-attach-buildtag) turned on in v3 rollout, appended compile tag to serialized canonical key -> misses. Mitigation = revert flag + runtime shim + CI test + Dedicated migration.

leo: Action items: sam merge runtime shim (urgent), compiler flag revert merge (nina), add CI invariant test (leo), infra migration ticket (ashley).

nina: Thanks team. I'll post perf dashboards and close the alert once we see stable metrics for 2 hours. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: alert resolved: prefix_cache_hitrate normalized. Link: https://perf.internal/alerts/AC-489/resolved
